A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 17 readable pages including Appendices A–D. Pages 2–17 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; page 1 differs only in author/contact formatting and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original NLI experiments on TOEFL4 and Write & Improve in Tables 1 and 4, an expert-component ablation in Table 2, and error analysis in Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablation results, and error analyses, including the Write & Improve results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 4.3.2 retains the same syntax, lexical, and idiomatic experts followed by a final language-identification expert. Their procedures and Appendix C prompts are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate English learner texts from TOEFL4 and Write & Improve for French, German, Italian, and Spanish native-language identification. The unmodified, supportive-signature, supportive-stereotype, misleading-signature, and misleading-stereotype scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Direct prompting and NER-redacted direct prompting remain the two baselines in Tables 1 and 4. Comparator participation across Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, and Kimi-K2 is identical.

E3.justification: Both retain the 440-essay TOEFL4 subset, balanced 400-essay Write & Improve sample, identical hint construction and redaction procedures, and macro-F1 evaluation. Model configurations and generation settings in Section 4.2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The single-expert ablation in Table 2, confusion-matrix error analysis in Figure 3, and robustness comparisons under supportive and misleading hints are identical. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and cross-condition volatility measure. Table 4 specifies three independent runs in both versions; no run-count or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All result entries, plotted findings, and accompanying empirical observations are unchanged, including Appendix D. For example, Table 1 retains Llama-3.3-70B agentic macro-F1 scores of 73.7 without modification and 73.1 with misleading stereotypes.

T1.justification: The definitions and reasoning concerning self-consistency and task decomposition are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations that differ between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about superficial-clue reliance, the inadequacy of simple mitigation strategies, and improved robustness and consistency through agentic decomposition.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretation of the peak-accuracy versus robustness tradeoff and the same explanations of expert behavior. Limitations concerning adversarial sophistication, dataset representativeness, and English-only evaluation are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access information, Groq generation settings, SpaCy model, dataset licensing details, approximately 150 Euro compute budget, task hints, and complete prompts are unchanged in the main text and Appendices A–C.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical. No cited work is added or removed, and positioning relative to prior NLI, faithfulness, and task-decomposition research is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page contact template changes from '<firstname>.<lastname>@uzh.ch' to '{firstname.lastname}@uzh.ch', and the arXiv version/date text is updated. Scientific prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 1 has small author-block spacing and alignment changes and a repositioned arXiv margin stamp. Figures 1–8, Tables 1–4, and all subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes only small first-page formatting and version-stamp updates. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and appendices are preserved, with no meaningful net effect on overall paper quality.
